resolution.summary: Replace MATLAB's built-in control_msgs definitions with those of the external ROS installation (Kinetic) through the custom-message workflow (rosgenmsg), instead of editing the MD5Checksum constant in the generated MATLAB class.
resolution.evidence: Answer by Cam Salzberger, 2021-01-19 (https://www.mathworks.com/matlabcentral/answers/394613-rosactionclient-failure-due-to-version-mismatch#answer_601519): "Changing the MATLAB files that define the message object does not change the underlying message definition, nor will it have an impact on the back-end that does the serialization of the message." and "The correct way to handle this is to replace the standard messages that MATLAB uses to match the message definitions used by your external version of ROS. Before R2020b, MATLAB uses ROS Hydro/Indigo message definitions. Follow these instructions to update built-in message definitions using the custom message workflow." The reporter never confirmed a fix; a later commenter (2020-08-03) wrote "I am facing tha same problem. Did u solve it ?".

notes: md5 evidence (genmsg rule applied to the generated ActionResult 'Header header / actionlib_msgs/GoalStatus status / FollowJointTrajectoryResult result', with actionlib_msgs GoalStatus/GoalID from common_msgs 1.12.6): control_msgs 1.2.0 gives bce83d50f7bb28226801436caf0e2043, the md5 the MATLAB client requests; 1.3.0 through 1.5.0 give c4fb3b000dc9da4fd99699380efcc5d9, the server's. The only change to FollowJointTrajectory.action between 1.2.0 and 1.4.0 is the added result field 'string error_string' (commit d758652, 2014-02-17), so the goal and feedback definitions agree and only the result topic is affected. 1.2.0 is the Hydro-era release; Indigo's control_msgs (1.3.x) already has error_string, so of the "Hydro/Indigo" definitions MATLAB states, the requested md5 matches Hydro's. consumer_built_against labels are inferred from these md5 matches; the source does not name control_msgs versions. The server's own package (for the UR10 Gazebo arm_controller) is not named in the source; control_msgs stands in as the provider because it holds the mismatched definition. The reporter's attempted workaround (replacing MD5Checksum = 'bce83d50...' with 'c4fb3b00...' in FollowJointTrajectoryResult.m) left the error unchanged; the answer explains why. The artifact's consumer sections quote the client code and the connection record with md5 fields removed plus the answerer's statements about MATLAB's definitions; the provider section [[control_msgs@1.2.0]] holds FollowJointTrajectory.action verbatim at that tag (the ActionResult/Result messages are generated from it). www.mathworks.com returned HTTP 403 to direct requests; the page was read from the Wayback Machine snapshot.
